name: Large language models

conventions.text: Draw a mixture-of-experts layer as one row of identical small numbered expert boxes with a router box beneath it; put a tiny bar chart of router scores beside the router and carry the selected scores along dashed curved arrows to circled-times gates above the chosen experts.

Draw a layer or block bottom-to-top: input hidden states or tokens at the bottom edge, the stacked sublayers above, the output at the top, so the figure reads like the transformer diagrams it extends.

In a comparison figure, draw the prior training or fine-tuning setup and the proposal as parallel panels in one shared visual vocabulary, with the proposal last (rightmost or bottom), so the reader can count what changed: models dropped, a loop removed, copies replaced by small add-ons, or one extra mechanism.

Draw the reinforcement-learning or feedback stage as a closed loop that returns into the model being trained, set apart from the one-pass steps by curved or dashed arrows while the one-pass steps keep straight solid ones.

Show preference data as candidate responses with their order made explicit: two response bubbles joined by a '>' sign with a trophy on the winner, or a column of response pills each paired with a score pill in a matching shade.

Show text data as one real, short example instead of a box labelled 'data': a quoted prompt above the data icon, a tabbed card with filled-in instruction / input / output fields, or the actual tokens of one example in a row.
Draw a token or hidden vector as a short strip of empty square cells: a row for a token entering a layer, or a column for one time step's vector.
Put the words of one example under the token positions, one word per position, so the token slots or cell rows read as language rather than as abstract vectors.
Show 'one per task / channel / sample' as a fan of two or three offset copies of the same card behind the front one, instead of drawing separate boxes.

In a multi-stage training pipeline, give data and processing steps different shape kinds (data as pale icon circles or tabbed example cards, steps as diamonds or clip-art icons) and name each stage with its own heading ('Step N: ...' or an uppercase pill tab) above or on the edge of its part of the figure.

source: summarised from the evidence cards listed under each convention
